restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Sections 8 and 18 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, and t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. Members are those of the winner sub-class (proof.md 18.1): phase (1, 0, 1) of the class of eta, e1 = 070c0307 + (W AND f8107cf8), with a five-bit slot from bits 0, 1, 2, 8 and 9 of W. A proposal that passes the exact fourteen-outcome filter runs one leaf path of the joint solver, named by its slot in a static envelope of at most 24 candidates, with the guards (G7) and (G15) proved lossless on all fourteen outcomes; every listed good trial owns one slot, so a proposal succeeds with probability exactly Zwin / 32 (Lemma SL32). Heuristic part: B = 23,225,324,486,506,309,197,923 proposals succeed with probability at least 0.3919693 under H1prime-winner-rate and H4prime-winner-pass-budget, with no dependence premise (proof.md 18.9).

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) per unit, 64 registers, constants as immediates (proof.md Section 11). A batch of seven packed proposal lanes with direct-table filter reads costs 341 (J = 3,317,903,498,072,329,885,418 batches); an E path 13 (B + 1 charged); a passing lane 512 plus the proved path cap 5,864 (L + 1 = 133,331,764,175,634,439,638 charged); once 550,029,492,264; the selection procedure SEL by construction, 8,882,224,365,081,579,520 operations; the final step 430 * 2^38. N = 2,283,466,521,894,204,308,690,142 machine units, T <= N / 430, log2 T = 72.16930706, checked in integers (proof.md 18.11). No sorting, no lookup by value; the direct tables (2^38 bytes) are built once.

Randomized by fresh uniform input bits: seven 32-bit words, a member field and a five-bit slot per lane, lanes made of disjoint bits (proof.md Lemmas PL and PLw). Success holds only under H1prime-winner-rate and H4prime-winner-pass-budget and is not measured. The organizer-run experiments run the search of proof.md 18.3 at toy scale (256 batches per seed) on the root instance of the construction (counter 0, flags 11): the winner member, the fourteen-outcome filter, the 32-slot sampler with (G7), (G15) and the certificate; no digest experiment can show the half-collision of a non-root chunk. The path cap and the direct-table batch are proved allowances of a specified layout, and the program's own ledger is higher (proof.md 18.14). No full 2-round collision is exhibited.

The six constants, eta, the beta* cube, the fourteen filter values and the winner phase, with the root-instance words, are a fixed nonuniform advice record of 124 bytes printed in proof.md Section 12. By Lemma ADV the budgets, the success bound and the time rows use only properties of this record that proof.md proves or counts exactly; no premise states what a procedure returns. The selection procedure SEL that finds the record is charged by construction as preprocessing inside time_log2: every run capped, 8,882,224,365,081,579,520 operations, below 2^54.198 units; preprocessing_log2 55 bounds it. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers the search with its direct tables (below 2^39 bytes), SEL (below 2^34 + 2^20 bytes) and the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), all held at once. No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical, winner-specific (proof.md 18.9), unchanged from entry 08444427. Let Zwin be the number of valid trials (t != 0) of one proposal of the winner sub-class (proof.md 18.1, Lemma PLw) that complete the collision with an E1 outcome among the fourteen of beta*, counted over all of Q* whether or not the proposal passes the filter. Rate: E[Zwin] >= mu = (2^21 - 1) * 5 * 9297 / (7 * 2^104), five sevenths (margin 1.4) of the exact model rate pwin = 9297 / 2^104 per trial. This is the whole premise; it states no dependence clause. The no-hit bound is derived from it: by Lemma SL32 a passing proposal certifies a collision at its own uniform slot with probability exactly Zwin / 32 (every listed good trial owns one of 32 slots, and at most 24 exist, Lemma B24), the slot bits are fresh bits of the proposal, and the proposals are independent, so over B = 23,225,324,486,506,309,197,923 proposals no hit has probability at most exp(-B * mu / 32) <= exp(-1/2) + 0.001, since B >= 4 B0 / 9 with B0 = 52,256,980,094,639,195,695,325 the run length of entry 08444427, for which B0 * mu / 72 >= -ln(exp(-1/2) + 0.001).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 18: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, E1.c1 drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, the member e1 = 070c0307 + (W AND f8107cf8) of phase (1, 0, 1) and y = e1 - Y3, seven proposal lanes per batch from disjoint fresh input bits, t solved per trial and t = 0 skipped; Zwin counts all of Q* in every proposal.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the exact count of the winner phase (proof.md 18.4): the cells of the parity certificate (P*) by phase, an exact enumeration, with the winner phase recounted with the counting program of Section 17, give the part 76,161,024 = 9297 * 2^13 on the scale 2^80, so pwin = 2^11 * 76,161,024 * 2^-128 = 9297 / 2^104 under the seven-word model, conditioned on the cube by Lemma S1 (which holds for any fixed set of members), taken at five sevenths. The lanes have disjoint inputs and each has the ordinary winner law exactly (Lemma PLw), so the packing adds no dependence. Participant evidence of Section 13 (real 32-bit counter trials matching the model on measurable partial events; a reduced-width end-to-end run) concerns the class and the sub-class of entry 26ebba63 and is untrusted by the harness; no measurement of the winner sub-class is claimed. The joint event, about 2^-91.3 per trial at the premised rate, is not measured at 32 bits.
heuristics.limitations: The rate, the factor five sevenths of pwin, is assumed; it has not been measured on the winner sub-class. No dependence clause is assumed: the 32-slot sampler makes the success of a proposal a 0/1 variable with mean exactly Zwin / 32 (Lemma SL32), so no bound on how successes cluster inside a proposal is needed. The organizer-run experiments run the search at toy scale on the root instance (counter 0, flags 11) and measure neither the rate nor the counter half-collision.

heuristics.statement: Supporting, winner-specific (proof.md 18.9), unchanged from entry 08444427. With pi_ow the probability that one proposal of the winner sub-class passes the filter of the fourteen outcomes: Pr[Bin(B0, pi_ow) <= L0] >= 0.9995, that is, with probability at least 0.9995 at most L0 = ceil(17 * B0 * pi14 / 16) = 299,996,468,082,244,789,290 of B0 = 52,256,980,094,639,195,695,325 independent proposals pass (pi14 = 1,520,837,058,143 / 2^48, about 2^-7.532). The run of this entry is shorter, B = ceil(4 B0 / 9); by Lemma PT (proved, by Hoeffding's inequality) the premise implies pi_ow <= (L0 + s0) / B0 with s0 = ceil(sqrt(B0)), and then more than L = ceil(B (L0 + s0) / B0) + ceil(sqrt(10 B)) = 133,331,764,175,634,439,637 passes occur with probability at most exp(-20). Reaching L halts the run with failure; the time bound charges L + 1 passing lanes and does not depend on this premise.
heuristics.scope: The fourteen-outcome filter of proof.md Section 8 on independent proposals of the winner sub-class (proof.md 18.1, Lemma PLw): the number of passing proposals among B0, binomial with B0 independent steps and the sampler's pass probability pi_ow.
heuristics.extrapolation: pi14 is the exact share for independent uniform pairs (Y9, Y3 + Y4 + w8), with a certificate in proof.md Section 8. If the sampler's pass probability is at most 1.06 pi14, the Chernoff bound puts more than L0 passing proposals below exp(-10^13). The product-model share alone is not a proof of this premise. A participant walk of real outer steps of the class with this filter measured 2^-7.5324 against 2^-7.5320 (proof.md 10.3; untrusted by the harness), with members from a part of the class.
heuristics.limitations: That the sampler's pass share is at most (L0 + s0) / B0, about 1.0625 pi14, is not proved, and it has not been measured on the winner sub-class. The time bound and the exactness of the filter do not depend on it.
